correctness.rationale: PASS: Summing internal spins on each path yields endpoint weights P_±=prod_i(1±s_i t^{ell_i}), with correlation (P_+-P_-)/(P_++P_-), denominator positive for 0<t<1. Base numerator factorization -2t²(1-t²)²(1+t²+t⁴)Q(t) was recomputed exactly, as were all 19 coefficients of transformed (1+z)^18 Q(z/(1+z)). There are exactly two Descartes sign changes. Direct exact signs of the numerator at t=7/10,3/4,4/5 are -,+,-, proving exactly two simple roots with no extra tangency. The signed inverse-tanh sum is negative as t->0 and t->1 and positive at 3/4; increasing either negative long path length preserves positivity there, giving >=2 roots for every 9<=d<e. For <=3 paths, two positive and one negative reduction gives a polynomial with two positive sign variations, including the simple t=1 root, thus at most one interior root. Independent direct spin enumeration on a small three-branch graph checked path elimination. The finite d,e grid in the package is not used to infer the infinite family.

originality.rationale: The signed-terminal-correlation law of a series-parallel theta network is standard. The checked potential new theorem is an equal-absolute-coupling *five*-path Ising network with exactly two finite-temperature sign changes, an infinite family with at least two, and a three-path impossibility boundary. Primary decorated-bond work has known nonmonotonicity and a single-crossing example but no inspected result implying the two-root 25-vertex example. Priority is best-of-knowledge, not exhaustive.

The result does not classify four-path graphs and the extended family has at least, not exactly, two crossings.

value.rationale: PASS: Reentrant sign of two-terminal thermal correlation under frustration is a natural observable; exactly two reversals with *identical absolute couplings* and no magnetic field identify a nontrivial topological entropy-competition mechanism. The rigorous Descartes root-count certificate and at-most-three-branch comparison give meaningful structural boundaries; a single approximate 25-vertex witness alone would not suffice.

final_claim: For five internally vertex-disjoint u-v paths with lengths (2,3,4,d,e), 9<=d<e, equal-magnitude zero-field Ising couplings whose path signs are (-,+,+,-,-), the endpoint correlation has at least two sign-changing positive-temperature zeros. The (d,e)=(9,10) example has exactly two simple zeros t≈0.706737737193050 and 0.799199522193006 for t=tanh(J/T). At most three paths of equal bond magnitude can have at most one reversal.
limitations: Exactly two zeros proved only for path lengths (2,3,4,9,10); lengthened instances need only at least two.
No four-branch classification or all-graph minimality; no thermodynamic phase transition in these finite graphs.
Specialized signed-series-parallel effective-coupling literature might have an unlocated dominating theorem.
